title: POC weekly sync - model selection and pinning (Orion Retail)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review latest benchmark results across candidate models and discuss pinning strategy and fallback rollouts. Redwood shared updated p50/p95 latency numbers and cost estimates, discussed canary vs immediate pin, and agreed next steps for staging latency tests and security docs. Action items assigned for pricing, staging test schedule, and QPS stress test plan.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Evan Brooks: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll give a quick agenda \u000B numbers review, model pinning proposal, fallback plan, and next steps. Priya's on to walk numbers.
[00:00:20] Aisha Khan: Great thanks Evan, we've got Daniel and Marta here as well.
[00:00:28] Priya Desai: Cool, I pulled the latest from the benchmark spreadsheet \u000B link: benchmark_spreadsheet_v3.xlsx \u000B and summarized p50/p95 across the catalog variants you asked about. Note: some of the labels in the sheet got munged during export, you'll see "redwood-v2-small" shows up as r-v2-s sometimes.
[00:00:45] Daniel Reyes: Yep we saw that, no worries. Can you call out the winner for latency first?
[00:00:52] Priya Desai: Sure \u000B for hosted endpoints the model we recommended last week, open-llama-70b-q4 (quantized), hits about p50 210ms p95 720ms at your typical 7-token prompt distribution in our staging runs. The smaller rwl-7b-int8 has p50 ~95ms p95 ~320ms but quality delta on longer completions is noticeable on your multi-turn checkout flows.
[00:01:20] Aisha Khan: How confident are we in those p95s \u000B were these measured with KV cache warm?
[00:01:26] Priya Desai: Good question \u000B these were mixed runs: 60% cold, 40% warm to reflect your real traffic. We can re-run a fully warm KV cache scenario, which would drop p95 by ~20-30% for the larger models. There was some jitter in the p95 due to occasional tokenization mismatches in the harness \u000B transcription note, there's a couple mis-encoded prompts in the sheet.
[00:01:52] Marta Silva: From product we care most about 99th user experience on long dialogues, so p95 is useful but we want to catch worst-case.
[00:02:00] Priya Desai: Understood, we can run a dedicated long-dialogue pass and push p99 numbers. For cost, the q4 70b variant is about 3.2x cost per token vs the 7b int8 in our cost model given your batching patterns.
[00:02:18] Evan Brooks: That matches last week's ballpark. Our recommended approach for this week is to pin model to open-llama-70b-q4 on hosted for the mid-tier flow, but put a fallback to rwl-7b-int8 for degraded regions or when latency exceeds the SLO. Proposal: canary the pin to 10% traffic for 48 hours, monitor user-visible score, then move to 100% if no regressions.
[00:02:40] Daniel Reyes: How will fallback behave? Will it change the output style? We're worried about inconsistent responses.
[00:02:48] Priya Desai: Fallback will be constrained: same system prompt and instruction tuning. The larger model may produce slightly more verbose completions; we can apply a post-processing normalization layer to trim verbosity where necessary. Also we can store a fallback flag in the response metadata so you can detect and surface a small notice in UI if needed.
[00:03:10] Aisha Khan: Are we able to pin specific model versions? We need immutability for compliance and reproducibility in the POC report.
[00:03:18] Evan Brooks: Yes, Redwood supports version pinning down to the model revision hash. We'll include the exact version id in the rollout plan and in the audit log. We'll also export the model hash for your records.
[00:03:30] Marta Silva: On security, next step was to get SOC2 + network diagram. Any update?
[00:03:36] Evan Brooks: We're attaching the security summary \u000B sec_summary_redwood.pdf \u000B and a network diagram for the private deployment option. We also included KMS key integration notes and logging retention options.
[00:03:50] Daniel Reyes: Cool. For the dedicated vs hosted discussion, did you simulate reserved capacity behaviors? Our traffic spikes could exhaust hosted quotas.
[00:03:58] Priya Desai: We ran a synthetic QPS spike in staging at 2x expected peak; hosted scaled and latency degraded gracefully with automatic fallback to the smaller model. For production, we recommended a Dedicated pool if you want strict throughput guarantees \u000B that's a separate contract line item.
[00:04:18] Aisha Khan: For the POC, we preferred to stay hosted but with some form of hard fallback threshold.
[00:04:24] Evan Brooks: That's fine. We'll implement an automatic fallback when p95 crosses 900ms or CPU/GPU queue length crosses configured threshold.
[00:04:32] Priya Desai: Quick note \u000B quantization profiles differ by kernel and hardware. On your staging nodes we saw slightly worse int4 artifacts on long token sequences; for safety we stuck with q4 on the 70b variant.
[00:04:46] Marta Silva: Any competitor compare we should call out? We ran a test last month vs Anthropic's Claude-internal and saw similar latency but better cost on your setup.
[00:04:56] Evan Brooks: Right, Anthropic was mentioned and OpenAI for baseline, but the benefit here is being able to pin versions and run private deployments if needed.
[00:05:04] Daniel Reyes: Let's talk about rollbacks \u000B if we detect regression in quality after a pin, what's the fastest route to rollback?
[00:05:11] Priya Desai: We support instant rollback to the previously pinned version via the control plane; you can set an automated rollback policy to revert to previous revision on metric regression (e.g., >5% drop in correctness eval). The rollback is near-instant in routing terms, though some in-flight requests may still hit the old model for a short period.
[00:05:30] Aisha Khan: How do we measure the correctness eval? We have a prompt set for checkout flows.
[00:05:36] Evan Brooks: We'll hook your eval prompt set \u000B you mentioned ~500 prompts \u000B to the canary pipeline and run them every 6 hours during the canary window. If F1/accuracy drops, automated alert and potential policy action.
[00:05:48] Marta Silva: Who will own the eval runs?
[00:05:51] Priya Desai: Redwood can run them but recommend your ML lead (Aisha) to own threshold decisions. We'll surface results in the vault & dashboard.
[00:06:02] Daniel Reyes: About instrumentation, can you push trace hooks so we can correlate user sessions to model responses?
[00:06:08] Evan Brooks: Yes we have tracing headers; we'll share the tracing integration doc and sample code.
[00:06:14] Priya Desai: There's a practical note \u000B some token counts in our harness were off because of your preprocessor doing a second pass of the prompt. We flagged the mismatches in the spreadsheet.
[00:06:26] Aisha Khan: We'll review the preprocessor.
[00:06:29] Priya Desai: For next testing steps I'd propose: 1) run a full warm-KV pass for p99 numbers; 2) run the 500 prompt eval against the canary model; 3) run a 2x QPS stress test to validate fallback triggers.
[00:06:42] Evan Brooks: Agreed. Also we recommended turning on continuous batching with a 50ms batching window to reduce cost while keeping latencies acceptable for synchronous flows. That gave a ~15% cost reduction in our tests.
[00:06:57] Marta Silva: Any expected change in tokenization or hallucination risk when switching to q4 70b?
[00:07:03] Priya Desai: Hallucination risk was lower on the larger model in our canonical prompts; quantization didn't materially increase hallucination for q4 but int4 showed more instability. We'll include hallucination metrics in the eval.
[00:07:20] Daniel Reyes: For observability, will we get per-route breakdowns and token-level cost?
[00:07:25] Evan Brooks: Yep, Redwood Console can show per-route token breakdowns, cost, p50/p95, and trace links. We'll give you a short demo next week.
[00:07:34] Marta Silva: Okay \u000B can you remind me of the canary window and traffic split?
[00:07:38] Priya Desai: Proposal: 48-hour canary, start at 10% traffic, monitor every 6 hours against your 500-prompt eval. If stable, 100% after 48 hours. If regression, auto-rollback and notify.
[00:07:52] Aisha Khan: Sounds good. For compliance we need the exact model hash in the POC report.
[00:07:57] Evan Brooks: We'll include the model revision hash and the deployment manifest in the POC artifact package.
[00:08:04] Daniel Reyes: Any gotchas with private deployment that might affect version pinning?
[00:08:09] Priya Desai: On Private, kernels and quantization artifacts depend on the target GPU drivers; we recommend running a quick compatibility compile step when moving from hosted to private \u000B that step is quick but mandatory for reproducibility.
[00:08:23] Marta Silva: Good to know.
[00:08:26] Evan Brooks: Quick Q for you \u000B are you comfortable with the fallback flag in responses showing to users, or do you want it only in logs?
[00:08:33] Aisha Khan: Prefer logs only for now. We'll revisit if UX sees major hit.
[00:08:38] Priya Desai: Noted. We'll leave the fallback metadata in logs and not surface to users by default.
[00:08:43] Daniel Reyes: On pricing: can you send updated reserved capacity options if we decide Dedicated later?
[00:08:49] Evan Brooks: Yes I'll attach the reserved capacity pricing sheet and tier options.
[00:08:54] Marta Silva: For actionables \u000B what's coming from Redwood in the next 72 hours?
[00:08:58] Priya Desai: We'll run the warm-KV p99 pass and push updated numbers and the 500-prompt eval results.
[00:09:05] Evan Brooks: I'll send pricing and security docs and propose a canary schedule.
[00:09:10] Aisha Khan: We'll review the preprocessor tokenization and confirm the prompt set is ready.
[00:09:15] Priya Desai: One minor transcript note \u000B the harness had a typo calling the 70b variant "open-lama-70b" in one column. Ignore that column.
[00:09:25] Marta Silva: Thanks, that explains earlier confusion.
[00:09:28] Evan Brooks: Any other questions?
[00:09:31] Daniel Reyes: Not from me.
[00:09:33] Aisha Khan: All good.
[00:09:35] Evan Brooks: OK we'll recap next steps and share artifacts. Thanks everyone.
[00:09:40] -- End of recorded portion --

Note: Transcript has typical Fireflies artifacts \u000B occasional mislabels and minor transcription errors.
